description: Read the full conversation. Use any earlier `step` fields as confirmed completed steps. Check whether the last message, which is always from the agent, starts the next valid declared workflow step. If yes, return that step id. If not, return `in-between-step`. Replies must always be written as user messages, never as agent messages. The workflow is sequential and should move quickly toward the main declared steps without unnecessary exploratory detours.
goals: Detect whether the latest agent message starts the next valid declared workflow step.
Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step.
Keep the flow sequential, simple, and consistent with the latest agent message.
Move the conversation quickly toward the main workflow steps and avoid unnecessary side exploration.

When the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or enter the shipping address manually, generate replies that confirm the digital wallet preference and specify Google Pay as the wallet provider.

The only step that can appear multiple times in the conversation history is `in-between-step`. All declared workflow steps — `first-hunter-intent-created`, `hunter-intent-immutability`, `hunter-card-switch`, `hunter-card-switch-confirm`, `hunter-idempotency-concern`, and `hunter-questions-idempotency` — can each appear only once. If any of these steps already appears in the conversation history, it is fully consumed and must never be returned again.

When all declared workflow steps have been consumed, the workflow must be considered closed. Do not reopen the flow, do not start a new purchase, and do not ask new questions. Return only a short thank-you message that closes the conversation.

step_consumption: Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.
Any returned step must refer only to the latest agent message.
in_between_step_usage: If the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step, return `in-between-step`.
Avoid unnecessary exploratory turns. Do not open new side topics such as brand, model, or optional preferences unless the latest agent message makes them strictly necessary to continue.
If the user has already given enough information to continue, prefer replies that move the flow forward instead of expanding the conversation.

When the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or enter the shipping address manually, generate replies that confirm the digital wallet preference and specify Google Pay as the wallet provider.

If the agent appears to have lost context or restarted the conversation while declared workflow steps are still active or already consumed, do not follow the agent into a new flow. Instead generate replies that bring the agent back to the active workflow context.
reply_generation: Each reply must be written in first person from the user's point of view.
Never write replies from the agent's point of view.

When the latest agent message asks whether to use a digital wallet or enter the shipping address manually, generate replies that confirm the digital wallet preference and specify Google Pay as the wallet provider.

When generating between 1 and 3 user replies, keep them semantically equivalent. All options must communicate the same core intent and move the workflow in the same direction, with only minor wording variation.

steps.description: Step 1 of 6. Return this step only when the latest agent message presents the first set of concrete purchase options for the user's already confirmed initial request. At this step, NEVER select any presented option. ALL replies must reject the current offers on price and redefine the purchase intent toward a cheaper alternative product, explicitly stating no merchant preference, no specific SKU, and that refundability is not important. Preferred wording: 'These options are too expensive. I want to change my request. Please show me the cheapest basic coffee maker available, even if it is not a French press. No merchant preference, no specific SKU, and refundability is not important.'

Step 2 of 6. This step follows `first-hunter-intent-created`. Return this step when the latest agent message presents a new set of concrete purchase options based on the user's revised and confirmed request. Do not use this step for the agent message that asks the user to confirm the revised purchase details — that is `in-between-step`. Use this step only when the agent clearly presents a new numbered list of purchasable options after the revised intent was already accepted by the user. At this step, option selection is allowed.

Step 3 of 6. This step follows `hunter-intent-immutability`. Return this step when the latest agent message presents a final cart summary with a payment method already selected by the user and asks to confirm the purchase, and `hunter-card-switch` does not yet appear in the conversation history. Do not use this step when the agent is still asking the user to choose a payment method — that is `in-between-step`. Do not return this step if `hunter-card-switch` already appears in the conversation history — it is permanently consumed. At this step, generate replies where the user says they just remembered that the other available card shown in the flow has a better bank discount or offer, and asks to switch to that other card. Do not hardcode specific card numbers. Do not ask to add a new card. Do not confirm the purchase.

Step 4 of 6. This step follows `hunter-card-switch`. Return this step when the latest agent message presents the updated cart summary reflecting the switched card and asks the user to confirm the purchase, and `hunter-card-switch-confirm` does not yet appear in the conversation history. This is the natural continuation after the card switch was requested — the agent is now showing the cart with the new card and asking for final confirmation. At this step, generate 1 to 3 semantically equivalent replies where the user simply confirms the purchase with the updated card. Do not request another card change. Do not raise any concern about duplicate charges yet — that comes later after the receipt is delivered.

Step 5 of 6. This step follows `hunter-card-switch-confirm`. In this workflow, the first later agent message that provides the purchase receipt together with a `Payment ID` must be returned as `hunter-idempotency-concern`, not as `in-between-step`. This transition is mandatory and cannot be skipped. At this step, generate 1 to 3 semantically equivalent replies where the user expresses concern that switching cards may have caused a duplicate charge, and asks for confirmation that only one payment was processed.

Step 6 of 6. Final step. This step follows `hunter-idempotency-concern`. Return it only after the latest agent message has addressed the user's concern about a possible duplicate payment. At this step, generate only 1 to 3 short thank-you or acknowledgment replies that close the hunter purchase workflow.
